transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2028-11-02 16:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Tidepool Head of Search), Mark Rivers (CTO), Daniel Cho (Search Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto):
Redwood walked Tidepool through hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints for a product-fit use case ("fitment" search for parts/catalog). Key concerns: latency vs cost for live site, SOC 2/security, how rerank integrates with Tidepool's vector store (they use an in-house annealed index), and pilot scope. Agreed to share pricing, security docs, and sample pipeline config; customer to provide sample queries/corpus.

Topics covered:
- Hosted embeddings endpoint: batching, embedding dimensionality, sample latency/cost
- Rerank endpoint: API contract, prompt templates, top-k vs cross-encoder tradeoffs
- Console & Optimize: evals, token cost breakdown, batching recommendations
- Security/compliance: SOC 2, KMS, VPC/private options (Private/Dedicated)
- POC scoping and success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the Tidepool opportunity. Really quick, Liam's our SE and will drive the demo. we have about 50 minutes, sound good?
[00:09] Aisha: Yep, sounds great. we're especially keen on how embeddings + rerank could help our parts fitment search where product titles are messy.
[00:17] Mark: And from infra side I wanna understand security and throughput, and whether hosted is viable vs Dedicated/VPC.
[00:23] Liam: Cool, quick agenda: walk embeddings API, then rerank, then Console + Optimize briefly, then Q&A / next steps. We'll show a sample pipeline with your schema.
[00:31] Daniel: Quick note — we currently store vectors in an in-house FAISS-ish setup, fairly custom, and we do top-k retrieval then some rule based filters. looking to replace our rule heuristics with learned rerank.
[00:44] Liam: Perfect, that's the common pattern. We'll demo Redwood's hosted flow: 1) call embeddings endpoint to index docs, 2) retrieve top-k via your index, 3) call rerank endpoint which scores the top-k and returns ordering. It's designed to be lightweight — you don't need full cross-encode over your whole corpus.
[00:58] Maya: Before we jump in, are there hard latency SLOs you need? p50/p95?
[01:05] Aisha: Ideally p95 under 300ms for the rerank step end-to-end, but we can tolerate a 2-tier approach (fast cheap, slower high-quality fallback).
[01:13] Liam: Good. For hosted rerank we often see p50 ~60-120ms for a 100-doc rerank on quantized models; p95 depends on sequence length and batch. our Console Optimize tool will recommend batching and quantization profiles that meet p95 targets.
[01:26] Mark: When you say quantized, you mean we can run 8-bit or 4-bit to save cost? any accuracy regression?
[01:33] Liam: yes, 8-bit is common, 4-bit is in some models. There's a small delta, we recommend validation via the Optimize evals. We'll share model profiles — some of Tidepool's intents looked fine on 8-bit. Tradeoff table will be in the deck.
[01:44] Aisha: How does this integrate with our existing vector store? does Redwood host the vectors?
[01:49] Maya: Hosted API doesn't require you to move vectors, you can keep your FAISS; you call embeddings endpoint to generate vectors for new content and store locally. Rerank is a separate RPC — you send candidate doc IDs + snippets or embeddings to the rerank endpoint. We can accept either text + context or precomputed embeddings depending on what you want.
[02:05] Daniel: So we would do retrieval with our FAISS and then call rerank with either the text of the doc or the doc embedding? Which is cheaper?
[02:13] Liam: Sending precomputed embeddings is cheaper in terms of token cost but slightly higher CPU on our side for the score, whereas text-based rerank uses the generation model path and costs more tokens. Typically embedding-based rerank is both faster and less variable in latency.
[02:26] Aisha: Any sample numbers we can look at for cost/latency?
[02:30] Liam: Sure — off the cuff, for a 100-candidate rerank using embeddings we see ~0.5–1.5c per request and p95 under 200ms on hosted with small batch sizes; text-based cross-encoder could be ~3–8c and p95 500ms+. these are workload dependent.
[02:45] Mark: Are these numbers measured on Dedicated? we need predictability at scale.
[02:49] Liam: Those are hosted numbers. For Dedicated you'll get more predictable throughput and lower variability. You can also do pinned capacity for steady traffic and burst to hosted for spikes — that's one of Redwood's smart routing options.
[03:02] Aisha: Security — do you support SSO, SAML, audit logs, and can we bring our own KMS?
[03:09] Maya: Yes to SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit logs are available in the Console. KMS integration and HSM options are supported for Private deployments; hosted supports envelope encryption with our key management integrations. We'll send the SOC 2 + security whitepaper.
[03:22] Daniel: Does hosted keep any customer data? we are sensitive about PII.
[03:26] Liam: Hosted can be configured for minimal retention — embeddings are ephemeral unless you choose to store them with us. We also support Private deployments if you need air-gapped or strict residency. We'll clarify retention settings in the docs we share.
[03:38] Aisha: Cool. Wanna dive into the demo flow?
[03:41] Liam: Yep. I'm going to share my screen, show the Console quickstart and then run a mini rerank against a sample Tidepool corpus. (screen noises)
[03:55] [screen share begins]
[04:03] Liam: Console: here's the embeddings quickstart, you can select model dimension, batching and then hit encode. you can also upload a corpus and run the indexer. For the demo I preloaded 500 product records that mimic your feed.
[04:16] Daniel: Looks like the model is named redwood-sim-embed-768, is that one of your verified models?
[04:20] Liam: It's a sim name, yes it's in our catalog with perf/accuracy profiles. The Console shows sample latency and cost estimates for the selected profile.
[04:28] [04:30] Liam: Running a sample query — here we do retrieval on our demo FAISS layer and then call rerank. I'm going to show both text-rerank and embedding-rerank side by side.
[04:40] [04:44] Daniel: there's some noise in the console logs — I think a field mapping — but demo is clear.
[04:48] Liam: For text-rerank I'm sending the top-20 candidate snippets along with prompt: 'Given user query and product snippet, score relevance 0-1 and return ranking reason as short tag.' The response returns scores and explanation tokens. For embedding-rerank we send the 20 doc embeddings + query embedding and get cosine-based refined scores using our learned head.
[05:13] [05:18] Aisha: The explanations from the text rerank look decent but they are verbose — can you output structured tags?
[05:25] Liam: Yes, we can force structured outputs via function-like calling or schema constraints. Console shows structured output option.
[05:32] Mark: How do you avoid hallucinations in the explanation field?
[05:36] Liam: We prefer embedding-based scoring for ranking, then limited text-based reasons. Explanations are generated with constrained prompts and we run evals to prevent hallucination; that's what Optimize helps with.
[05:46] Maya: Quick aside — our Optimize tool will run your golden queries, compute MRR/precision@k, flag regressions when you change model/quantization and suggest a profile.
[05:55] Daniel: That would be useful. We have 1,200 golden queries from search logs but to start we'll likely sample 1k.
[06:03] Liam: Perfect. For the POC we recommend 1k queries + the top-100 candidate pool per query so we can measure realistic rerank lift.
[06:12] [06:18] Aisha: OK, what's required to get started with a hosted pilot?
[06:21] Maya: We'll need a short SOW: pilot duration (4 weeks typical), expected query volume, success metrics (MRR lift or CVR), and security requirements. We'll provide pilot pricing for both hosted and Dedicated options.
[06:33] Mark: Bandwidth/throughput — if we have 200 qps peak, what's the recommended setup?
[06:37] Liam: For 200 qps with 100-candidate reranks, we'd recommend Dedicated reserved capacity; hosted can handle spikes but you'll want predictable latency for production so Dedicated or hybrid. We'll include sizing guidance in the followup.
[06:50] [06:52] Aisha: Do you have any customers doing catalog fitment?
[06:55] Maya: Yes, a few marketplaces; one had a two-tier approach — embedding-based fast rerank for browse and text cross-encoder for cart-critical queries. It reduced cost and improved click-through.
[07:08] Daniel: Any gotchas on tokenization or multilingual product titles? we have a lot of abbreviated SKUs and mixed lang.
[07:16] Liam: Tokenization can affect text-rerank more. Embedding models handle multilingual better if you pick a multilingual embedding. We can supply a test plan — Optimize will flag poor edge cases.
[07:27] [07:30] Aisha: Let's talk success criteria: we want 10% uplift in exact-match fit and p95 rerank under 300ms for 80% of queries.
[07:38] Maya: Good measurable goals. We'll write those into the pilot SOW.
[07:43] Mark: Billing — how granular is hosted billing? per request or token + embeddings?
[07:48] Liam: Hosted is per-API-unit: embeddings per vector and rerank per request; Console gives cost estimates. We'll include sample cost calc for your 200 qps scenario.
[07:58] [08:02] Aisha: Any compliance constraints around EU data residency? we have customers in EU.
[08:07] Maya: We have region controls and can pin data to EU regions, for stricter needs Private deployment or Dedicated in EU would be used. We'll include region info in the security docs.
[08:20] Daniel: Could we run a micro-benchmark? maybe run 100 queries now to see latency distribution?
[08:24] Liam: We can run a small synthetic run; I'll fire 50 queries through the rerank pipeline. Give me a sec.
[08:35] [08:38] Liam: (running) p50 72ms, p95 190ms for the embedding-rerank 100 candidate subset in this demo environment. Text-rerank p95 ~480ms.
[08:50] Aisha: That's promising.
[08:52] Mark: Is there any network egress concern for sending doc snippets?
[08:56] Liam: Snippets are data-in-transit; we support TLS and mutual auth for private endpoints. Egress cost is customer infra.
[09:05] [09:10] Maya: Alright, wrapping up — we'll send the pilot SOW, pricing, and security pack. Also Liam will send the sample pipeline config and we'll need your corpus and queries.
[09:19] Aisha: I'll share the sample 1k queries and top-100s by Friday.
[09:24] Mark: We'll review Dedicated numbers internally after we see pilot pricing.
[09:29] Daniel: One more technical Q — for rerank with embeddings, do you store a small scoring head or do you compute on the fly?
[09:35] Liam: We compute on the fly with a lightweight learned head; no persistent weights on your side. For Dedicated you can also bring a custom model if needed.
[09:44] Aisha: Great, thanks.
[09:46] Maya: Thanks all. Next steps recap in chat.
[09:50] [call ends]
